title: SDL Revision Mock Marathon — Upper Limb, Histology & Embryology
content:
# SDL Revision Mock Marathon — Upper Limb, Histology & Embryology

*Spot-style revision set, University of Nairobi. Scope: upper limb gross anatomy, histology and embryology. 50 questions.*

## Q1: Name the nerve labelled N and state its root value
![Q1 - dissection of the axilla with a nerve tagged N](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q01.jpg)

**Answer:** Musculocutaneous nerve. Root value: C5, C6, C7 (from the lateral cord of the brachial plexus).

## Q2: State two muscles innervated by the nerve tagged
![Q2 - same axillary dissection, nerve tagged](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q02.jpg)

**Answer:** Coracobrachialis and biceps brachii (it also supplies brachialis — any two).

## Q3: Name the vessel tagged and state its extents
![Q3 - forceps tagging a vessel in the deltopectoral/axillary region](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q03.jpg)

**Answer:** Cephalic vein. It begins in the roof of the anatomical snuffbox at the wrist, runs up the lateral forearm and arm, passes through the deltopectoral groove, then pierces the clavipectoral fascia to drain into the axillary vein.

## Q4: State the root value of the nerve tagged and two muscles it innervates
![Q4 - probe tagging a nerve root at the supraclavicular fossa](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q04.jpg)

**Answer:** Suprascapular nerve; root value C5, C6. Supplies supraspinatus and infraspinatus.

## Q5: State the root value of the nerve tagged and its distribution
![Q5 - probe tagging a nerve root near the brachial plexus roots](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q05.jpg)

**Answer:** Long thoracic nerve; root value C5, C6, C7. Runs down over the outer surface of serratus anterior, which it supplies.

## Q6: State innervation and two actions of the muscle that inserts in the part shown
![Q6 - proximal humerus with an attachment site pinned](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q06.jpg)

**Answer:** Supraspinatus, inserting on the greater tuberosity of the humerus. Innervation: suprascapular nerve (C5, C6). Actions: initiates/assists abduction of the shoulder (first 15°) and stabilises the humeral head in the glenoid (part of the rotator cuff).

## Q7: Name the muscle X and state its innervation
![Q7 - digitated muscle on the lateral chest wall marked X](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q07.jpg)

**Answer:** Serratus anterior. Innervation: long thoracic nerve (C5, C6, C7).

## Q8: Name two contents of the space probed
![Q8 - probe inserted between two converging fan-shaped muscles](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q08.jpg)

**Answer:** The apex/floor of the axilla region shown here transmits the axillary vessels and cords/branches of the brachial plexus — name any two, e.g. axillary artery and the cords of the brachial plexus.

## Q9: Name a muscle that (a) originates and (b) inserts on the part probed, and state their innervation
![Q9 - two fan-shaped muscles converging at a probed point](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q09.jpg)

**Answer:** Pectoralis major (origin: clavicle/sternum/costal cartilages — medial and lateral pectoral nerves, C5–T1) and pectoralis minor (inserts on the coracoid process — medial pectoral nerve, C8, T1).

## Q10: State the origin and innervation of the muscle probed
![Q10 - probe on a fan-shaped chest wall muscle](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q10.jpg)

**Answer:** Pectoralis major — origin: medial half of clavicle, sternum and upper costal cartilages. Innervation: medial and lateral pectoral nerves (C5–T1).

## Q11: Identify structure A and ligament B
![Q11 - labelled dissection, structures A and B](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q11.jpg)

**Answer:** A: a branch/cord of the brachial plexus in the axilla. B: coracoclavicular ligament (trapezoid/conoid parts) — verify letters against the source image before publishing.

## Q12: State 2 actions of E and origin of F
![Q12 - forearm dissection, E and F labelled](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q12.jpg)

**Answer:** E (biceps brachii): flexion of the elbow and supination of the forearm. F (brachialis): origin from the anterior surface of the distal humerus.

## Q13: State 4 sites of entrapment of A
![Q13 - probe tagging a nerve at the medial elbow, labelled A](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q13.jpg)

**Answer:** A = ulnar nerve. Sites of entrapment: (1) arcade of Struthers, (2) the medial intermuscular septum, (3) the cubital tunnel (behind the medial epicondyle, between the two heads of flexor carpi ulnaris), (4) Guyon's canal at the wrist.

## Q14: State the termination of the artery labelled V
![Q14 - artery labelled V in a forearm/cubital fossa dissection](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q14.jpg)

**Answer:** Brachial artery — terminates in the cubital fossa, at the level of the neck of the radius, by bifurcating into the radial and ulnar arteries.

## Q15: State the neurovascular structure most at risk due to a fracture at the tagged part and give the basis
![Q15 - humerus with the surgical neck pinned](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q15.jpg)

**Answer:** Axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral vessels. Basis: they wind directly around the surgical neck of the humerus through the quadrangular space, so a fracture here can stretch or lacerate them.

## Q16: Identify structures A and B
![Q16 - shoulder MRI with A and B labelled](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q16.jpg)

**Answer:** A: subscapularis tendon. B: supraspinatus tendon.

## Q17: State the structure tagged and its clinical utility
![Q17 - pin at the cubital fossa](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q17.jpg)

**Answer:** Median cubital vein. Clinical utility: the standard site for venepuncture and IV cannulation.

## Q18: State 2 ligaments associated with the joint probed
![Q18 - probe at the elbow joint](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q18.jpg)

**Answer:** Ulnar (medial) collateral ligament and radial (lateral) collateral ligament of the elbow.

## Q19: Identify structures 3, 4, 5 and 7
![Q19 - wrist X-ray with carpal bones numbered](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q19.jpg)

**Answer:** 3: triquetrum. 4: trapezium. 5: trapezoid. 7: hamate.

## Q20: Name the structures A, B, C and D
![Q20 - forearm dissection with A, B, C, D labelled](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q20.jpg)

**Answer:** A: median nerve. B: a branch of the musculocutaneous nerve (lateral cutaneous nerve of forearm) or brachial vessels at the elbow. C and D: cutaneous branches/vessels of the forearm — verify letters against the source image before publishing.

## Q21: Name the terminal branches of the structure below
![Q21 - palmar dissection with a probe](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q21.jpg)

**Answer:** Superficial palmar arch (formed mainly by the ulnar artery) — terminal contributions: three common palmar digital arteries and a proper palmar digital artery to the little finger.

## Q22: Identify the muscle tagged and its action
![Q22 - probe on a fan-shaped chest wall muscle](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q22.jpg)

**Answer:** Serratus anterior. Action: protracts the scapula and rotates it upward (essential for full abduction/flexion of the arm above the horizontal).

## Q23: State the communications of the space labelled X
![Q23 - diagram of the palm with a fascial space labelled X](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q23.jpg)

**Answer:** Midpalmar space. Communicates proximally with the space of Parona in the forearm (via the carpal tunnel), and distally with the web spaces/dorsum of the fingers via the lumbrical canals.

## Q24: Identify the nerve below and its nerve roots
![Q24 - forearm dissection, central nerve](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q24.jpg)

**Answer:** Median nerve; roots C6–T1 (contributions from the lateral and medial cords of the brachial plexus, ultimately C5/6–T1).

## Q25: State two muscles that form the floor of the space below
![Q25 - labelled cubital fossa prosection](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q25.jpg)

**Answer:** Cubital fossa — floor formed by brachialis and supinator.

## Q26: Name the branches of the structure labelled X
![Q26 - probe tagging a nerve/vessel in the proximal forearm](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q26.jpg)

**Answer:** Radial nerve, dividing into a superficial (sensory) branch and a deep branch (posterior interosseous nerve) near the elbow, at the level of supinator.

## Q27: Identify the tagged bone and a muscular attachment to it
![Q27 - wrist skeleton with a carpal bone tagged X](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q27.jpg)

**Answer:** Pisiform. Muscular attachment: flexor carpi ulnaris inserts on it (abductor digiti minimi also originates from it).

## Q28: State two actions of the tagged muscle
![Q28 - probe on a wrist tendon](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q28.jpg)

**Answer:** Flexor carpi radialis — flexion of the wrist and abduction (radial deviation) of the wrist.

## Q29: Identify the muscle below and its innervation
![Q29 - thenar eminence dissection](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q29.jpg)

**Answer:** Abductor pollicis brevis. Innervation: recurrent (motor) branch of the median nerve.

## Q30: State (a) the site of entrapment of the nerve below at the wrist, (b) its nerve roots
![Q30 - nerve at the wrist crease](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q30.jpg)

**Answer:** Median nerve. (a) Carpal tunnel, deep to the flexor retinaculum. (b) Roots C6–T1.

## Q31: State two characteristic features of the tissue displayed
![Q31 - skeletal muscle histology](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q31.jpg)

**Answer:** Skeletal muscle — visible cross-striations, and multiple peripherally-located (subsarcolemmal) nuclei per fibre.

## Q32: Giving reason, identify the epithelial type displayed
![Q32 - ciliated epithelium over cartilage](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q32.jpg)

**Answer:** Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium (respiratory epithelium of the trachea). Reason: all cells rest on the basement membrane, but not all reach the free surface, so nuclei appear at different levels giving a falsely stratified look; cilia are visible on the luminal surface.

## Q33: Identify A and B
![Q33 - skeletal muscle fibres with A and B labelled](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q33.jpg)

**Answer:** A: peripheral nucleus of a skeletal muscle fibre. B: myofibrils showing cross-striation.

## Q34: Identify zones labelled A and D
![Q34 - epidermis histology with zones a and d](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q34.jpg)

**Answer:** A: stratum granulosum. D: stratum basale (germinativum).

## Q35: State two sites where the tissue displayed is found
![Q35 - mucoid connective tissue around a small vessel](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q35.jpg)

**Answer:** Mucous (mucoid) connective tissue — found in Wharton's jelly of the umbilical cord and in the dental pulp of a developing tooth.

## Q36: Name 1, 2, 3 and 4
![Q36 - electron micrograph of a sarcomere](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q36.jpg)

**Answer:** 1: Z-line (Z-disc). 2: A-band. 3: I-band. 4: a sarcomere (Z-line to Z-line).

## Q37: Give the salient features of the tissue displayed
![Q37 - cartilage-type histology](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q37.jpg)

**Answer:** Hyaline cartilage — chondrocytes sit in lacunae (often as isogenous groups), the matrix is basophilic/metachromatic (rich in chondroitin sulfate), the tissue is avascular, and it is bounded by a perichondrium (absent at articular surfaces).

## Q38: Identify epithelium displayed and where it is found
![Q38 - epithelium histology, source image is damaged/incomplete](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q38.jpg)

**Answer:** The image is corrupted/incomplete in the original source file — only a small strip of low cuboidal-to-columnar epithelial cells survives, not enough to confirm the specific type with confidence. Recommend sourcing a clean replacement image before publishing.

## Q39: State major collagen types in the tissue displayed
![Q39 - dense regular connective tissue histology](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q39.jpg)

**Answer:** Tendon (dense regular connective tissue) — predominantly type I collagen, with a minor contribution of type III collagen in the surrounding endotenon.

## Q40: Name cell types found in region a
![Q40 - testis histology with region a marked](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q40.jpg)

**Answer:** Seminiferous tubule: spermatogenic cells at various stages (spermatogonia, primary/secondary spermatocytes, spermatids) and Sertoli (sustentacular) cells.

## Q41: State the anomaly depicted and give its basis
![Q41 - grape-like translucent vesicles](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q41.jpg)

**Answer:** Hydatidiform mole (molar pregnancy). Basis: hydropic (cystic) degeneration of chorionic villi from an abnormal conceptus — a complete mole (androgenetic, diploid, empty ovum fertilised by a duplicating sperm) or partial mole (triploid, from dispermy).

## Q42: State the anomaly depicted and give its basis
![Q42 - conjoined infants](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q42.jpg)

**Answer:** Conjoined twins. Basis: incomplete splitting of the embryonic disc during monozygotic twinning after day 13, leaving the twins joined at a shared body region.

## Q43: Identify X and state a structure related to its formation
![Q43 - sagittal MRI of the lower spine showing a sac-like mass](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q43.jpg)

**Answer:** X: a spina bifida cystica sac (meningocele/myelomeningocele). Related structure: failure of closure of the neural tube (posterior neuropore) during the fourth week.

## Q44: State the anomalies labelled A and B
![Q44 - diagram comparing two spina bifida variants](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q44.jpg)

**Answer:** A: meningocele (herniation of meninges and CSF only, no neural tissue in the sac). B: myelomeningocele (meninges and neural tissue/spinal cord herniate into the sac).

## Q45: Identify A and B
![Q45 - two placental specimens](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q45.jpg)

**Answer:** A: fetal (chorionic) surface of the placenta, showing umbilical vessels branching beneath the amnion. B: the umbilical cord and its vessels dissected off the placental disc, with a marginal (battledore) insertion.

## Q46: State the procedures labeled A and B
![Q46 - diagrams of two prenatal sampling procedures](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q46.jpg)

**Answer:** A: transabdominal chorionic villus sampling (ultrasound-guided needle through the maternal abdomen into the chorionic villi). B: transcervical chorionic villus sampling (catheter passed through the cervix under ultrasound guidance).

## Q47: Identify placental attachment depicted in A & B
![Q47 - diagram of umbilical cord insertion sites on the placenta](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q47.jpg)

**Answer:** Variations in umbilical cord insertion on the placenta — A: eccentric (paracentral) insertion. B: marginal (battledore) insertion, at the edge of the placental disc.

## Q48: State 2 functions of B
![Q48 - trilaminar embryonic disc diagram, primitive node, A and B labelled](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q48.jpg)

**Answer:** B: (intraembryonic) mesoderm. Functions: gives rise to the musculoskeletal, cardiovascular and urogenital systems; forms the notochord (from the primitive node), which induces overlying ectoderm to form the neural tube.

## Q49: Identify the anomaly and state its basis
![Q49 - newborn with a large umbilical mass](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q49.jpg)

**Answer:** Omphalocele (exomphalos). Basis: failure of the herniated midgut to return to the abdominal cavity by the 10th week (or failure of the lateral body-wall folds to fuse at the umbilical ring), leaving abdominal viscera herniated into the cord base, covered by a peritoneal/amniotic sac.

## Q50: Identify the anomaly and state its basis
![Q50 - H-shaped diagram of the gut tube and a diverticulum](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/sdl-mock-marathon/q50.jpg)

**Answer:** Meckel's diverticulum. Basis: incomplete obliteration of the vitelline (omphalomesenteric) duct, which normally connects the midgut to the yolk sac and regresses by week 7.

---
*Compiled from a University of Nairobi student SPOT-question collection ("Aponeurosis 01"), originally assembled by Jose Kariuki (Jitu) with contributions from department lecturers, demonstrators and students. Answers without an inline source answer were researched and written for this collection; flagged items should be double-checked against a primary source before publishing.*

title: PAT III — Progress Assessment Test (8 November 2019)
content:
# PAT III — Progress Assessment Test (8 November 2019)

*Spot-style revision set, University of Nairobi, Dept. of Human Anatomy. 50 questions, upper limb, histology and embryology, with answers.*

## Q1: Name the tagged nerve and state its root value
![Q1 - dissection of the arm with a nerve tagged](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q01.jpg)

**Answer:** Medial brachial cutaneous nerve; root value C8, T1.

## Q2: State two muscles innervated by the nerve tagged
![Q2 - axillary dissection, nerve tagged](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q02.jpg)

**Answer:** Coracobrachialis, brachialis (medial part) and biceps brachii.

## Q3: Name the vessel tagged and state its extents
![Q3 - forceps tagging a vessel in the axilla](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q03.jpg)

**Answer:** Axillary artery; extends from the lateral border of the first rib to the inferior border of teres major.

## Q4: State the root value of the nerve tagged and two muscles it innervates
![Q4 - probe tagging a nerve at the shoulder](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q04.jpg)

**Answer:** Axillary nerve; root value C5, C6. Supplies deltoid and teres minor.

## Q5: State the root value of the nerve tagged and its distribution
![Q5 - probe tagging a nerve in the axilla](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q05.jpg)

**Answer:** Intercostobrachial nerve (lateral cutaneous branch of the 2nd intercostal nerve); root value T2. Distribution: skin of the floor of the axilla and upper medial arm.

## Q6: State innervation and two actions of the muscle that inserts in the part shown
![Q6 - humerus with an attachment site pinned](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q06.jpg)

**Answer:** Latissimus dorsi, inserting on the intertubercular (bicipital) groove of the humerus. Innervation: thoracodorsal nerve. Actions: medial rotation, extension and adduction of the shoulder.

## Q7: Name the muscle X and state its innervation
![Q7 - back dissection, muscle marked X](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q07.jpg)

**Answer:** Longissimus (part of erector spinae). Innervation: dorsal rami of spinal nerves.

## Q8: Name two contents of the space probed
![Q8 - probe in the deltopectoral triangle](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q08.jpg)

**Answer:** Deltopectoral triangle — contains the deltoid branch of the thoracoacromial artery, the cephalic vein, and the deltopectoral (infraclavicular) lymph nodes.

## Q9: Name a muscle that (a) originates and (b) inserts on the part probed, and state their innervation
![Q9 - scapula specimen with a probed point](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q09.jpg)

**Answer:** (a) Coracobrachialis and the short head of biceps brachii originate from the coracoid process — musculocutaneous nerve. (b) Pectoralis minor inserts on the coracoid process — medial pectoral nerve.

## Q10: State the origin and innervation of the muscle probed
![Q10 - probe on a chest wall muscle](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q10.jpg)

**Answer:** Subclavius. Origin: 1st costochondral junction. Innervation: nerve to subclavius.

## Q11: Identify A and B
![Q11 - shoulder dissection with A and B labelled](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q11.jpg)

**Answer:** A: long head of biceps brachii tendon. B: coracohumeral ligament.

## Q12: State 2 actions of E and origin of F
![Q12 - arm dissection, E and F labelled](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q12.jpg)

**Answer:** E (biceps brachii): flexion of the elbow and shoulder; supinates the forearm when the elbow is midflexed. F (medial cord of the brachial plexus): roots C7, C8, T1.

## Q13: State 4 sites of entrapment of A
![Q13 - probe tagging a nerve at the arm, labelled A](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q13.jpg)

**Answer:** Radial nerve — arcade of Frohse, the spiral (radial) groove of the humerus, the lateral intermuscular septum, and between brachialis and brachioradialis.

## Q14: State the termination of the artery labelled V
![Q14 - artery labelled V in a forearm dissection](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q14.jpg)

**Answer:** Ulnar and radial arteries (brachial artery terminates by bifurcating into these two at the level of the neck of the radius, in the cubital fossa).

## Q15: State the neurovascular structure most at risk due to a fracture at the tagged part and give the basis
![Q15 - humerus with a fracture site pinned](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q15.jpg)

**Answer:** Brachial artery. Basis: it is tethered as it passes through the fibrous arch of pronator teres / distal humerus region and can be compressed or lacerated by displaced fracture fragments.

## Q16: Identify structures A and B
![Q16 - shoulder MRI with A and B labelled](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q16.jpg)

**Answer:** A: supraspinatus (tendon). B: acromion.

## Q17: State the structure tagged and its clinical utility
![Q17 - pin at the cubital fossa](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q17.jpg)

**Answer:** Median cubital vein; clinical utility: intravenous access/venepuncture.

## Q18: State 2 ligaments associated with the joint probed
![Q18 - probe at the elbow joint](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q18.jpg)

**Answer:** Quadrate ligament, annular ligament (and the radial collateral ligament).

## Q19: Identify structures 3, 4, 5 and 7
![Q19 - wrist X-ray with carpal bones numbered](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q19.jpg)

**Answer:** 3: pisiform. 4: trapezium. 5: trapezoid. 7: hamate.

## Q20: Name the structures A, B, C and D
![Q20 - forearm dissection with A, B, C, D labelled](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q20.jpg)

**Answer:** A: pronator quadratus. B: median nerve. C: anterior interosseous nerve. D: anterior interosseous nerve (accompanying vessels/second branch shown).

## Q21: Name the terminal branches of the structure below
![Q21 - palmar dissection with a probe](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q21.jpg)

**Answer:** Radial artery — princeps pollicis artery, radialis indicis artery, and the deep palmar arch.

## Q22: Identify the muscle tagged and its action
![Q22 - probe on a forearm muscle](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q22.jpg)

**Answer:** Brachioradialis; flexes the elbow joint, and supinates the forearm from a pronated position (to neutral/mid-flexed position).

## Q23: State the communications of the space labelled X
![Q23 - diagram of the palm with a fascial space labelled X](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q23.jpg)

**Answer:** Web space (interdigital) proximally continuous with the space of Parona distally, at the wrist/forearm.

## Q24: Identify the nerve below and its nerve roots
![Q24 - forearm dissection, central nerve](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q24.jpg)

**Answer:** Radial nerve; roots C5–C8, T1.

## Q25: State two muscles that form the floor of the space below
![Q25 - labelled cubital fossa prosection](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q25.jpg)

**Answer:** Brachialis and supinator.

## Q26: Name the branches of the structure labelled X
![Q26 - probe tagging a vessel in the proximal forearm](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q26.jpg)

**Answer:** Ulnar artery — common interosseous artery (dividing into anterior and posterior interosseous arteries), and the ulnar recurrent artery.

## Q27: Identify the tagged bone and a muscular attachment to it
![Q27 - wrist skeleton with a carpal bone tagged X](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q27.jpg)

**Answer:** Pisiform; the tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris attaches to it.

## Q28: State two actions of the tagged muscle
![Q28 - probe in the palm](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q28.jpg)

**Answer:** Lumbricals — extend the interphalangeal joints and flex the metacarpophalangeal joints.

## Q29: Identify the muscle below and its innervation
![Q29 - thenar eminence dissection](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q29.jpg)

**Answer:** Abductor pollicis brevis; innervated by the recurrent branch of the median nerve.

## Q30: State (a) the site of entrapment of the nerve below at the wrist, (b) its nerve roots
![Q30 - nerve at the wrist crease](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q30.jpg)

**Answer:** Ulnar nerve. (a) Guyon's canal. (b) Roots C7, C8, T1.

## Q31: State two characteristic features of the tissue displayed
![Q31 - skeletal muscle histology](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q31.jpg)

**Answer:** Skeletal muscle — cross-striations, multinucleated fibres, elongated cells with peripheral nuclei.

## Q32: Giving reason, identify the epithelial type displayed
![Q32 - ciliated epithelium over connective tissue](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q32.jpg)

**Answer:** Pseudostratified columnar ciliated epithelium. Reason: cilia are visible on the surface, and there is a lack of nuclei in the apical one-third of the epithelium (nuclei sit at varying levels, all cells reach the basement membrane).

## Q33: Identify A and B
![Q33 - bone histology with A and B labelled](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q33.jpg)

**Answer:** A: Haversian canal. B: osteocytes in lacunae.

## Q34: Identify zones labelled A and D
![Q34 - growth plate histology with zones a and d](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q34.jpg)

**Answer:** A: resting zone. D: zone of calcification.

## Q35: State two sites where the tissue displayed is found
![Q35 - mucoid connective tissue](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q35.jpg)

**Answer:** Wharton's jelly of the umbilical cord, dental pulp of a developing tooth, and the nucleus pulposus of the intervertebral disc.

## Q36: Name 1, 2, 3 and 4
![Q36 - electron micrograph of a sarcomere](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q36.jpg)

**Answer:** 1: Z-disc. 2: A-band. 3: M-line. 4: I-band.

## Q37: Give the salient features of the tissue displayed
![Q37 - cartilage histology](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q37.jpg)

**Answer:** Elastic cartilage — abundant elastic fibres in the matrix, and large lacunae housing chondrocytes.

## Q38: Identify epithelium displayed and where it is found
![Q38 - transitional epithelium histology](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q38.jpg)

**Answer:** Transitional (urinary) epithelium; found lining the renal calyces, ureters, and urinary bladder.

## Q39: State major collagen types in the tissue displayed
![Q39 - connective tissue histology](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q39.jpg)

**Answer:** Type I and type II collagen.

## Q40: Name cell types found in region a
![Q40 - bone marrow/ossification histology with region a marked](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q40.jpg)

**Answer:** Osteoclasts, osteocytes, osteoblasts, and osteoprogenitor cells.

## Q41: State the anomaly depicted and give its basis
![Q41 - grape-like translucent vesicles](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q41.jpg)

**Answer:** Molar pregnancy / hydatidiform mole. Basis: the paternal set of chromosomes outnumbers/predominates over the maternal set.

## Q42: State the anomaly depicted and give its basis
![Q42 - conjoined infants](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q42.jpg)

**Answer:** Conjoined twins (Siamese twins) — here, omphalopagus. Basis: incomplete separation of the embryonic disc at the primitive streak stage.

## Q43: Identify anomaly X and state an embryonic structure related to its formation
![Q43 - sagittal MRI of the lower spine showing a mass](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q43.jpg)

**Answer:** X: chordoma. Related structure: the notochord (chordomas arise from notochordal remnants).

## Q44: State the anomalies labelled A and B
![Q44 - diagram comparing two spina bifida variants](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q44.jpg)

**Answer:** A: spina bifida — meningocele. B: spina bifida — meningomyelocele.

## Q45: Identify A and B
![Q45 - two placental specimens](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q45.jpg)

**Answer:** A: battledore placenta (marginal cord insertion). B: velamentous insertion of the umbilical cord.

## Q46: State the procedures labelled A and B
![Q46 - diagrams of two prenatal sampling procedures](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q46.jpg)

**Answer:** A: amniocentesis. B: chorionic villus sampling.

## Q47: Identify placental attachment depicted in A & B
![Q47 - diagram of abnormal placental adherence](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q47.jpg)

**Answer:** A: placenta increta. B: placenta percreta.

## Q48: State 2 functions of B
![Q48 - trilaminar embryonic disc diagram, primitive node, A and B labelled](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q48.jpg)

**Answer:** B: endoderm — forms the primitive (embryonic) gut, and gives rise to primordial gut-derived epithelial cells/organs.

## Q49: Identify the anomaly and state its basis
![Q49 - compressed, mummified fetus](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q49.jpg)

**Answer:** Fetus papyraceus. Basis: death and compression/mummification of one fetus in a multiple pregnancy.

## Q50: Identify the anomaly and state its basis
![Q50 - H-shaped diagram of the gut tube and a fistulous tract](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/pat3-2019/q50.jpg)

**Answer:** Vitelline fistula. Basis: persistence of the vitelline (omphalomesenteric) duct, which normally obliterates by week 7.

---
*Compiled from a University of Nairobi student SPOT-question collection ("Aponeurosis 01"), originally assembled by Jose Kariuki (Jitu) with contributions from department lecturers, demonstrators and students. Answers transcribed directly from the original paper's answer key.*

title: Embryology Slide Review Marathon
content:
# Embryology Slide Review Marathon

*Numbered embryology identification set, sent 7 June 2017. Answers are the original compiler's answer key, matched to each numbered image by letter.*

## Number 1: Spermatogenesis — identify A–G
![Number 1 - diagram of spermatogenesis stages A to G](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n01.jpg)

**Answer:** A: spermatocytogenesis/mitosis. B: primary spermatocyte. C: first meiotic division. D: secondary spermatocyte. E: second meiotic division. F: spermatids. G: spermiogenesis.

## Number 2: Mature Graafian follicle — identify A–G
![Number 2 - histology of a mature Graafian follicle A to G](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n02.jpg)

**Answer:** A: corona radiata. B: zona pellucida. C: oocyte. D: follicular antrum. E: granulosa cells. F: theca. G: cumulus oophorus.

## Number 3: Identify A–C
![Number 3 - fertilised oocyte and blastocyst diagrams A to C](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n03.jpg)

**Answer:** Left image — A: zona pellucida. B: oocyte. C: polar body. Right image — A: blastocoel. B: trophoblast. C: embryoblast.

## Number 4: Implantation — identify A–H
![Number 4 - implanting blastocyst diagram A to H](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n04.jpg)

**Answer:** A: trophoblastic lacunae. B: syncytiotrophoblast. C: cytotrophoblast. D: amniotic cavity. E: epiblast. F: hypoblast. G: exocoelomic (Heuser's) membrane. H: umbilical vesicle.

## Number 5: Trilaminar disc (epiblast) — identify A–D
![Number 5 - trilaminar embryonic disc diagram A to D](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n05.jpg)

**Answer:** A: notochord. B: primitive pit. C: primitive node. D: primitive groove.

## Number 6: State the anomaly and its basis
![Number 6 - newborn with a sacrococcygeal mass](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n06.jpg)

**Answer:** Sacrococcygeal teratoma — failure of degeneration/regression of the primitive streak. (The compiler's own key leaves the follow-up "what cell types does it have" unanswered — a teratoma of this type typically contains tissue from all three germ layers.)

## Number 7: Identify A–L
![Number 7 - embryonic folding diagram A to L](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n07.jpg)

**Answer:** A: exocoelomic (Heuser's) membrane. B: intraembryonic coelom. C: intermediate mesoderm. D: neural tube. E: paraxial mesoderm. F: notochord. G: somatic (parietal) lateral mesoderm. H: splanchnic (visceral) lateral mesoderm. I: surface ectoderm. J: primordial gut. K: secondary umbilical vesicle. L: amniotic cavity.

## Number 8: Identify A–D
![Number 8 - neural tube formation diagram A to D](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n08.jpg)

**Answer:** A: surface ectoderm. B: neural folds. C: neural crest. D: notochord.

## Number 9: Identify labelled structures
![Number 9 - myotome diagram, epimere and hypomere](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n09.jpg)

**Answer:** Left diagram — A: epimere. B: hypomere. C: dorsal rami of spinal nerve. Right diagram — A: epimere. D: ventral rami of spinal nerve.

## Number 10: Name the anomalies (left to right)
![Number 10 - three anterior abdominal wall anomaly photos](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n10.jpg)

**Answer:** Prune belly syndrome — failure of migration and fusion of the anterior abdominal wall muscles. Poland syndrome — absence of pectoralis major. Congenital arthrogryposis — joint rigidity due to absent/underdeveloped muscles.

## Number 11: Chorionic villi and embryonic folding — identify labelled structures
![Number 11 - chorionic villi diagram and craniocaudal folding diagram](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n11.jpg)

**Answer:** Left diagram — A: secondary chorionic villi. B: trophoblastic lacunae. C: connecting stalk. D: amniotic cavity. E: umbilical vesicle. F: exocoelomic cavity. G: splanchnic lateral mesoderm. H: cytotrophoblast. I: syncytiotrophoblast.

![Number 11 (continued) - result of craniocaudal and lateral folding](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n11b.jpg)

**Answer (continued):** Right diagram (results of craniocaudal and lateral folding) — A: septum transversum. B: amnion. C: allantois. D: exocoelomic membrane.

## Number 13: Fetal membranes — identify labelled structures
![Number 13 - fetal membranes and decidua diagram](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n13.jpg)

**Answer:** Left diagram — A: smooth chorion. B: decidua capsularis. C: chorionic cavity. D: decidua parietalis. E: decidua basalis. F: chorion frondosum. G: amniotic cavity. H: secondary umbilical vesicle. Right diagram — I: amniochorionic membrane. J: amniotic cavity.

## Number 14: Identify the placental specimens
![Number 14 - several placenta specimens, normal and abnormal](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n14.jpg)

**Answer:** First row: bilobed (membranacea) placenta, battledore placenta. Second row: placenta previa, placenta accreta, placenta increta, placenta percreta.

## Number 16: The placenta
![Number 16 - placenta specimen with membranes doubled back](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n16.jpg)

**Answer:** Circumvallate placenta — the fetal membranes double back on themselves at the placental margin.

## Number 18: Identify the conjoined twin types
![Number 18 - four sets of conjoined twins](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n18.jpg)

**Answer:** Craniopagus, thoraco-omphalo-pygopagus, pygopagus, thoracopagus (as shown, left to right).

## Number 19: Skin development — identify labelled layers
![Number 19 - developing epidermis diagram](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n19.jpg)

**Answer:** A: surface ectoderm. B: mesenchyme. C: periderm. D: basal layer. E: mesenchyme.

## Number 20: Name the skin anomalies (left to right)
![Number 20 - seven skin condition photos](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n20.jpg)

**Answer:** Port-wine stain, cavernous haemangioma, hypertrichosis, ichthyosis vulgaris, albinism, alopecia, anonychia (absence of nails).

## Number 21: Mammary ridge and breast development
![Number 21 - milk line diagram and mammary bud development](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n21.jpg)

**Answer:** A: milk line / mammary ridge (mammary crest). Development sequence — A: surface ectoderm, B: mesenchyme, C: primary mammary bud, D: mammary pit, E: lactiferous duct.

## Number 22: Name the breast anomalies (left to right)
![Number 22 - six breast anomaly photos](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n22.jpg)

**Answer:** Polymastia, polythelia, inverted nipples, gynaecomastia, Poland syndrome (and amastia).

## Number 23: Limb bud development — identify labelled structures
![Number 23 - limb bud and pharyngeal arch diagram](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n23.jpg)

**Answer:** Left diagram — A: pharyngeal arches. B: developing heart. C: developing lower limb bud. D: somites. Right diagram — A: mesenchyme. B: zone of proliferation. C: apical ectodermal ridge (patterns limb bud growth in a proximo-distal axis). D: zone of polarizing activity (patterns limb bud growth in an antero-posterior axis).

## Number 24: Name the limb anomalies
![Number 24 - limb anomaly photos and X-rays](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n24.jpg)

**Answer:** Amelia, congenital absence of the radius, phocomelia, lobster-claw hand, limb amputation (constriction band), pre-axial polydactyly, club foot.

## Number 25: Name the skeletal anomalies (left to right)
![Number 25 - child with short stature, hip X-ray, hand anomaly photos](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n25.jpg)

**Answer:** Achondroplasia, syndactyly, congenital dislocation of the hip joint, polydactyly, macrodactyly.

## Number 26: Neural tube and brain vesicles — identify labelled structures
![Number 26 - neuropore diagram and forebrain-midbrain-hindbrain diagram](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n26.jpg)

**Answer:** Left diagram — A: cranial neuropore. B: somites. C: caudal neuropore. Right diagram — A: telencephalon. B: diencephalon. C: optic vesicles. D: mesencephalon. E: metencephalon. F: myelencephalon.

## Number 26b: Developing urogenital system — identify labelled structures
![Number 26 continued - developing kidney, ureter and bladder diagram](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n26b.jpg)

**Answer:** This diagram (developing metanephros, ureteric bud, and bladder) was not separately keyed in the original source — recommend cross-checking against a standard embryology text before publishing (labels broadly correspond to: A – developing kidney, B – renal pelvis, C – ureteric orifices, D/E – developing bladder and urogenital sinus).

## Number 27: Name the neural tube/cranial anomalies (left to right)
![Number 27 - eight photos of neural tube and cranial anomalies](/images/year1/anatomy/aponeurosis-01/embryology-slide-review/n27.jpg)

**Answer:** Raschisis, acrania coupled with anencephaly, spina bifida occulta, spina bifida cystica (meningocele), spina bifida cystica (myelomeningocele), hydrocephalus, microcrania, crania bifida.

---
*Compiled from a University of Nairobi student SPOT-question collection ("Aponeurosis 01"), originally assembled by Jose Kariuki (Jitu) with contributions from department lecturers, demonstrators and students. Answers transcribed from the original compiler's answer key (sent 7 June 2017); Number 15 and Number 17 have no corresponding entry in the source key and are omitted here rather than guessed. Number 26b's diagram wasn't separately keyed in the source and is flagged for review.*
